classification.evidence: modal-runtime is the core with a fan of three seams (worker gRPC: task input + control RPCs and events + management RPCs; task dispatch to the engine; filesystem HTTP over UDS to modal-daemon), and worker -> runtime / runtime -> worker is an anti-parallel pair of RPC relations between the same two boxes.
tie_breakers_considered: Density (E ~= N would favor flow-chains): 8 relations over 8 components is chain-like in count, but the relations are not one-per-node - modal-runtime is the tail of four of the eight - and the source's own signature is a 3-edge fan plus an anti-parallel pair. The candidate skill's family table lists modal-runtime under service-meshes, which settles the tie.
lifecycle-machines: no phases, stages or boot order appear in the source, and the source never animates anything, so the phase-rank and one-dot-per-transition recipe does not apply.

placement-planes: modal-runtime vs Blobnet/storage could be read as two worlds, but the source names no bus; every cross-boundary relation is a direct RPC (dispatch, mounts/snapshots, image+volume data, HTTP over UDS), so there is nothing to trunk.
identity-probe-maps: the eight components are named modules, not addresses, ports or qualifier-dense identifiers, so coverage-by-identifier is not the hard part.
classification.secondary_recipe_applied: none - the three views are a sizing split (skill Step 7: at 77x47 a wide graph needs two to four views), not a second family's recipe
